stage_a.note: The founders deliver a highly energetic, positive pitch with loud, confident voices and smiles.
They start with an energetic chant and maintain high excitement about their brand's mission.
They are friendly, approachable, and clearly proud of their mother-son partnership.

venture.description: An inspirational designer lifestyle apparel brand combining fashion and comfort for youth and adults.
venture.note: They emphasize the brand's positive, inspirational message for go-getters.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founders introduce themselves, state their ask, and pitch their inspirational clothing brand, sharing its origin and early success.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori invites the panel to check out the clothing samples in front of them.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond holds up a green sweatshirt and remarks on it.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark holds up a blue sweatshirt, calling it Mavs blue.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert asks Trey why the brand is called Spergo.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trey explains that the name combines the words sports and heroes, with 'go' added for go-getters.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark encourages Trey, showing appreciation for his explanation.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond compliments the quality of the clothing, noting that the logos are fully embroidered rather than patched.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trey thanks Daymond for the compliment on the quality.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert asks for the price of some of the clothing items.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sherell states that the cost to make the Leo sweatsuit is 21.50.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori asks what they sell the sweatsuit for.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sherell replies that the sweatsuits are sold for 170 dollars.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert remarks that it is a premium brand given the high retail price.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sherell confirms that they are indeed a premium brand.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori asks Trey to tell the story of how he sold out his first batch of t-shirts.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trey explains he used birthday money to buy shirts, sold them at local barbershops, and kept reinvesting to grow.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark asks Sherell to confirm that Trey woke her up every Saturday to go sell.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sherell confirms that he did.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori asks about Trey's initial daily sales goals.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sherell explains that Trey would quickly hit his initial goal and then continuously raise it to buy more inventory.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond asks what motivates people to buy the clothing with such passion.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trey says the brand is a feeling that inspires youth globally to chase their dreams at a young age.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks Trey if he has a large following on social media.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trey shares he has over 89,000 followers on his personal account and 71,000 on the business page.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori expresses amazement at his follower count.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori asks what initially led Trey to decide to create a clothing line.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trey explains that growing up around violence in Philadelphia inspired him to become a positive role model.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sherell adds that her own mother was a seamstress and that dressing well for church was a family tradition.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert expresses that he loves the origin story.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert asks what their total sales are to date.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trey reports that their total sales to date are 1.8 million dollars.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori is visibly impressed by the sales figure.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert asks for clarification on the period of time over which the 1.8 million was made.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trey provides a year-by-year breakdown showing rapid growth from 40k in 2018 up to 938k in the current year.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark expresses his amazement at the sales growth.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sherell adds that they currently sell through an e-commerce store and three pop-up shop locations.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark asks to confirm if they have three locations right now.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert asks what percentage of their total sales are from online e-commerce.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trey answers that 70% of sales are point-of-sale and 30% are e-commerce.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert says he is blown away by Trey speaking with the maturity of someone much older.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond asks where all the traffic and sales are coming from.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trey recounts meeting a contact who gave him Diddy's number, leading Diddy to post about him and drive massive traffic.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sherell adds that Diddy gave Trey a 25,000 dollar grant which they used to open their physical store.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond asks what they project their total sales will be for the current year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trey states they are planning to do 2.2 million dollars this year.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert asks how much profit they have made year to date.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sherell answers that their profit is 313,000 dollars.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks if that profit figure is before they pay themselves.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sherell clarifies that it is after they have paid themselves.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin is impressed by the net profit.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond asks what they intend to do with the requested investment money.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sherell says they want to hire a fashion designer and get help with digital sales to sustain their growth.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond challenges why they need an investor when they are already making 2.2 million on their own.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sherell explains they are behind on production seasons and feel ready to blow the company up with help.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond asserts they are already blowing up and questions if they are truly ready for a partner.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori praises them but feels she isn't the best partner for their specific needs, so she exits.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin calls Trey incredible but notes clothing is not his space, so he drops out.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert exits because their heavy reliance on brick-and-mortar retail scares him compared to online models.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark offers the requested 300k but asks for 25% equity, wanting to help guide the young superstar.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond asks Mark if he wants to partner up on the deal.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark declines, stating he doesn't need Daymond for this particular business.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond makes his own matching offer of 300k for 25%.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trey counters Daymond, asking if he would do 300k for 20%.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond quickly accepts Trey's counter offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trey accepts the deal with Daymond.

decisions.note: Feels she isn't the best partner for them despite finding them impressive.
Scared by their heavy reliance on brick and mortar rather than online sales.
Wants to help guide the young founder.
Matches Mark's offer after Mark declines to partner up.
Accepts the revised deal with Daymond.

record.notes: Several edits jump between different parts of the Q&A, particularly around sales figures and marketing.
